headline: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics resolve tumor microenvironment states and drivers
label: Tumor Microenvironment Transcriptomic Profiling
summary: Integrating single-cell and spatial profiles with bulk cohorts now links cellular context to prognosis and regulatory programs across cancers.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these studies is integration of single-cell or spatial transcriptomics with bulk cohort data to define prognostic states and regulators. The pancreatic study places OTUD7B within epithelial remodelling and a Treg-rich immunosuppressive microenvironment, while the cervical study uses 341,978 cells to identify epithelial subcluster epi8 and markers stratifying LSIL risk. A glioblastoma study shows a reduced spatial gene module recapitulating single-cell molecular classifications, and colorectal work pairs scRNA-seq with spatial data to tie CHPF and GPC1 to cancer-associated fibroblast-dominant domains. Other studies extend the approach to transcription factor architecture in NSCLC radiogenomics, multi-omics survival modelling, and SCITRAM for master transcription factor prediction from single-cell data. Not every item shares this design; several rely on bulk TCGA or proteomic data. What is new is convergence: regulatory, metabolic, and immune axes are increasingly resolved within the cellular context in which they operate.
